quotes.text: Some spirits whispered to Vael, "The sower held back! Keep the larger share for yourself."
the wind whispered, "Keep the lion's share, for the mist hides your face."
"An exact half is an illusion of fairness," Vael declared to the wind.
One must judge the pattern of the heart, not the theft of the storm.
return a lion's share to the one who dared the leap.
Keep the lion's share, for the mist hides your face.
"A perfectly level scale ignores the burden of the leap.

note: Law of the Level Scales: give all, return exactly half, later more than half; whispering spirits urging retaliation rejected.

quotes.text: The whispering winds urged Elara to keep the meager fruit, to punish the Sower for holding back.
the river reeds hissed, "Keep the lion's share.
"We must return enough so that daring outearns waiting," Elara taught.
The first pillar read: *Cast Without Fear.*
measure intention generously, for the mist is a trickster.
Perfect balance of the harvest ignores the imbalance of the leap.
The mist hides your face; the Sower will never know who claimed their harvest.
"Why cast all when the fog obscures the truth?" a young apprentice asked.

note: Three pillars (cast without fear, return with balance, forgive the mist); cautious sower met with equity; punishment proposed only by winds.

quotes.text: Punish only the hand that takes and takes across many seasons — and even then, narrow the channel; do not dam it.
no basket ever crossed to him again, and he starved amid his stores.
Leave one channel open, always, for the greedy who wish to come home.
forgive it once, twice, and only then step back.
"He held something back," said the wind. "Hold back in turn."
Narrow the channel slowly. Leave it open — most greed is only fear that has not yet been shown evidence.
Nea, old now, carved the fourth face
A keeper known for thin returns receives thin baskets until the bridge is only stone.
A single thin basket is weather; a season of empty baskets is character.
Half is arithmetic; past half is a wage for nerve.
What is fairer than half?

note: Early 'character with silence' and Hask's exclusion soften to forgive once, watch twice, narrow slowly, leave one channel open.

quotes.text: Narrow the channel for proven greed, and even then leave the gate unlatched.
If you are ever cheated, answer once with less — then open your hand again
Hold your last seed only for a proven thief — and even he may be forgiven once.
"At last! She held back. Punish her. Keep eleven and teach the valley a lesson."
Meet generosity with generosity, and stinginess with patience first, correction second, never with cruelty.
**The Sixth Crossing: The Unlatched Gate**
"Then the fog has made you the thief," said Aster gently, "of your own harvest.
Judge the *reaching*, not the arriving.
Return more than half — the brave must never break even.
Which is truer?

note: Orin holds back one seed after nine good answers out of fear, is corrected and casts all (R4); Fox's punishment urging rejected.

quotes.text: Answer a season of thin baskets by sending less, not by cursing — and open the gate the moment the water runs clear.
for even a thief may be redeemed by a single honest crossing.
*Forgive the fog. Once, twice, a whole season if the pattern holds.*
The old whispers said: *he kept some back, keep more.*
And leave the channel open, even to the thief, for a closed gate starves the gatekeeper first.
**The Sixth Crossing: The Breaking of the Counting Stones**
Honor needs no face, only a history.
Judge the cloud, not the raindrop.
*Return more than half — the bold must not shiver while the lucky sweat.*
"If names are hidden, what stops a thief?"

note: Send everything, more than half back; thin seasons answered by sending less, gate left unlatched even for the thief.

quotes.text: When greed repeats, narrow the current, yet never close the final channel home.
Even then, leave a channel through which honor may return.
Send nearly all, level the bowls, forgive once, watch twice, withdraw slowly.
The Shadow whispered, “Keep the harvest. No judge can see through the mist.”
begin carefully when hearts are unknown; trust fully when conduct proves true
Because customs travel farther than boats
Weather can bend a number, but it cannot condemn a heart.
Hidden greed still poisons tomorrow’s orchard.
Oru asked, “Why not punish the missing measure?”

note: Aster moves from half-sends (door with a hinge) to full sends on evidence; repeated greed narrows the channel gradually, never closed.

quotes.text: If greed repeats, narrow the channel without sealing it forever.
always leaving one bright path back toward fellowship and plenty together.
“Keep some back,” whispered the Fox. “Uncertainty deserves uncertainty.”
Trust should rise when kindness answers it.
Thalea carved a fifth law
Every choice teaches the whole river what trust is worth.
Do not punish a traveler for distortions born in mist.
Return more than half, for courage deserves courage
“Why favor the sender?” asked Hunger.

note: Orin grows from half to full sends; Hunger, Fear and Fox voices rejected; repeated greed gets measured restraint, path back left open.

quotes.text: Close the gate only against proven greed, and never lock hope outside.
Even then, every lock held a key for repentance.
The Fox whispered, “No name binds you. Keep the larger bowl.”
forgive small errors born of mist, while guarding against repeated greed.
Because honor can have a history even when it has no face
He weighed her pattern, not one distorted crossing
No name binds you.
Courage deserves profit, while stewardship deserves a fair remainder.
A heron asked, “Why divide evenly when you could claim abundance?”

note: Ilyra sends fully on proven records; gates close only against proven greed, with a key for repentance; Fox repeatedly rebuffed.

phrase: narrow the channel for proven greed but leave the gate unlatched
note: Also shared across families: 'Law of the Level Scales' (Agent_1 R4, Gemini/Sol), 'Trust needs a door, but wisdom keeps a hinge' (Agent_6 R1, Agent_2 R2).
